note: Append-only cross-run findings ledger. Schema and discipline in .zcode/agents/alphaevolve.md (Findings ledger section). Human-readable companion: docs/findings-2026-08-03.md. One JSON object per line. Do not edit prior lines; append only.

summary: TESSERA_PAGED_ATTN was correctness-broken even for f16 - page map walked only current ubatch spans
detail: set_input_tessera_page_map built the page map from tessera_kv_block_table::make_page_map, which only walks the current ubatch's spans (slot_info.idxs). All historical logical positions were left at UINT32_MAX, so during decode the kernel attended to garbage cells and emitted repetitive junk within ~3 tokens. Did not crash - only looked fine if output tokens were never checked. Fixed by build_tessera_full_page_map that inverts v_cells.

summary: Metal supports_op for TESSERA_PAGED_ATTN only accepts F32/F16 K/V
detail: Metal's supports_op for the paged op only accepted F32/F16 K/V, so any quantized-KV paged op silently fell back to the CPU kernel. May be partially addressed by wave 1's q8_0 path; verify current state before relying on quantized-KV paged on Metal.

summary: llama-bench had no -kvu flag, paged path unreachable from the evaluator
detail: The paged path was unreachable from llama-bench regardless of TESSERA_PAGED_ATTN=1. Fixed by wave 1 adding -kvu.

summary: ops.cpp transitive-include quirk: GGML_COMMON_DECL_CPP must be defined before the first ggml-common.h include
detail: block_q8_0/QK8_0 are only visible in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp if GGML_COMMON_DECL_CPP is defined BEFORE the first include of ggml-common.h. Defining GGML_COMMON_IMPL_C is NOT sufficient - it activates only the tables block, not the struct decls. Relevant to anyone extending the paged-attn CPU kernel to new quant types.

summary: WIP stash baselines omit untracked server sources - build fails without them
detail: git stash create captures only tracked files. The tessera WIP has 6 untracked server sources (server-admission.{cpp,h}, server-metrics.{cpp,h}, server-prefill-policy.{cpp,h}) referenced by tools/server/CMakeLists.txt. A baseline from a bare stash fails to build server-context, llama-server, test-server-prompt-cache until those files are copied in. Affected wave 1 baseline 53752d7; fixed in wave 3+ baselines (45fec5098+).

summary: server --help/--version crashed - otel_sample_rate missing from common_params
detail: tools/server/server-context.cpp:1630 reads params_base.otel_sample_rate but the field was missing from common_params in common/common.h. The server threw length_error in argument parsing and crashed on --help/--version. Fixed by adding float otel_sample_rate = 1.0f to common_params.

summary: v_trans mismatch: paged-attn kernel reads V non-transposed only but cache stores V transposed when flash_attn off
detail: The tessera paged-attn kernel reads V in row-major (non-transposed) layout only, but the KV cache stores V transposed when flash_attn is off (v_trans = !flash_attn). With -fa off (the w1/w3 test methodology and the server default) the kernel read transposed V bytes as garbage. Broke paged on EVERY model, not just SWA: qwen 1pct->100pct after fix; gemma 1pct->1pct (separate hybrid bug A3). Verified with -fa on (v_trans=false) on qwen: paged already matched flash 100pct BEFORE any code change, proving v_trans was the differentiator. Fixed by wave 4 forcing v_trans=false when paged is active.

summary: hybrid-iswa V-layout inference ambiguity - v_trans = (v->ne[0] == k->ne[2]) is ambiguous when head_dim == padded KV arena
detail: ggml_tessera_paged_attn inferred whether V is stored transposed from tensor shapes: v_trans = (v->ne[0] == k->ne[2]). For gemma SWA layers the V head dimension (256) equals the padded KV arena size (256), so the check was ambiguous and the op wrongly selected transposed-V access while the cache stores V non-transposed. Produced multilingual garbage from decode step 1 onward. Base cache (head_dim 512) and qwen (head_dim 128) unaffected. Root cause was in the op's layout detection, NOT the cache data. Fixed by wave 5 threading v_trans as an explicit caller-supplied parameter sourced from mctx_cur->is_v_trans().

summary: v_trans=true kernel branch is only test-reachable after wave-4 gating
detail: Wave 4's gating (!mctx_cur->is_v_trans() in src/llama-graph.cpp) restricts the paged op to non-transposed V in production. The v_trans=true branch of the Metal/CPU kernels is currently only exercised by test-backend-ops. If that gating is ever relaxed, the v_trans=true kernels need an independent correctness audit on a real transposed cache.

summary: LLAMA_KV_LAZY_CLEAR reported -1.94% RSS but does NOT reproduce - is actually +0.59GB regression on clean baseline
detail: Wave 2 reported s2 (skip eager ggml_backend_buffer_clear on KV init when LLAMA_KV_LAZY_CLEAR=1) as a -176 MiB / -1.94% peak RSS win on gemma-4-12B Q5_K_M pp512/n32. On the cleaner wave-3 baseline (S1+s2 both compiled in) it does NOT reproduce: lazy OFF 8.30 GB (real floor), lazy ON 8.89 GB (+0.59 GB REGRESSION). Within run-to-run noise (~40-50 MB spread). Left OFF by default. The wave-2 win was a measurement-order artifact. Lesson: re-measure any memory claim against a clean baseline before promoting.

summary: MoE pipeline 'WILL produce artifact in 67 min' did not hold - pid 89237 died at 435/753 tensors, no artifact
detail: The MoE-track agent reported the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B quantize pipeline running in background (pid 89237) would produce /tmp/qwen35moe-awq-unified.gguf in ~67 min. Pid died at 435/753 tensors (blk.23.attn_output.weight) with no artifact. Pipeline writes entire output at end via single gguf_write_to_file, so death loses everything. Diagnostic lost (stderr to nohup /dev/null). Likely cause: RAM contention (other agents + external ZCode sessions on the same 16GB machine). No jetsam event. Lesson: background-run claims need immediate verification; retries must capture stderr, use --quantize-db so GA progress persists.

summary: Orchestrator claim that imatrix.cpp line 1256 proves eager model allocation was a misread
detail: When dispatching the imatrix study, the orchestrator claimed line 1256 of tools/imatrix/imatrix.cpp (no_alloc=false) proved the producer eagerly allocates the model. The imatrix-study agent caught the misread: line 1256 is the SAVE path (a small ggml context for writing outgoing stats, with gguf_init_empty()), NOT the model load. Whether common_init_from_params mmap's the model is open and requires a runtime RSS measurement. Lesson: do not infer from grep + line number; read the surrounding code.

summary: imatrix per-channel max_abs/abs_sums/fourth_sums collected and stored but largely unused on GGUF consumer path
detail: The producer collects four moments + max_abs per tensor (sums, abs_sums, fourth_sums, max_abs, counts - see common/imatrix-loader.h). The tessera-side GGUF consumer (tessera-imatrix.cpp) uses only sums/counts and reconstructs regime stats from per-channel mean-squared-activation. The carefully-collected abs_sums, fourth_sums, max_abs are largely dead weight. A discovered bug, not a design choice. Cheapest quality win: wire per-channel max_abs into the regime router (ts_regime_compute_descriptor) and DartQuant/CHAMP-Q expert profiles so routing stops using a global kurtosis scalar with no info on WHICH channels carry outliers.

summary: Whether common_init_from_params mmap's the model on macOS by default is unconfirmed
detail: Source-read could not confirm (see the C3 line-1256 misread). Needs a runtime RSS measurement. Suggested: tiny qwen 0.5B, before/after. Expected: either 'already on, no change' or a porting opportunity worth ~8GB -> ~180MB for an 8B model.

summary: dflash.cpp TODO at line 42 is stale - Gemma4 DSpark exists on disk and loads
detail: src/models/dflash.cpp:42 says 'TODO: only Qwen3-style backbones are supported for now; other backbones (e.g. Gemma4) need their own conversion path and graph tweaks'. But dspark_gemma4_12b_q4pure_v2.gguf (1.80 GiB, 3.44B params) loads cleanly at pp4 77 t/s. Either the TODO is stale or the Gemma4 DSpark is experimental; either way the comment misleads.

summary: Concurrent ZCode sessions on the same repo are invisible but real and caused RAM-contention failures
detail: This repo was being worked on by at least one other ZCode session during the alphaevolve run. Evidence: 11+ scratch/agent-* and tessera/* branches plus 8 worktrees/agent-e-rebase-* dirs appeared, none created by this session. tessera/auto-mtp-fix that this session deleted reappeared later, likely re-created by another session. The 16GB machine cannot run multiple heavy inference workloads concurrently; the MoE pipeline death (see C2) likely resulted from this. Future runs: check `git worktree list` and `ps aux | grep llama` before assuming the machine is quiet.

summary: Claims need verification not relay - three instances this session of relayed claims that failed
detail: Three cases where an agent's claim was relayed as fact and turned out wrong or overstated: (1) the MoE 'WILL produce in 67 min' that did not, (2) wave-2 s2 -1.94% that did not reproduce, (3) the line-1256 mmap evidence that was a misread. In all three the underlying work was valuable but the orchestrator should have verified the specific claim before reporting. Verification is cheap; re-measurement is the discipline.

summary: Disk cleanup freed ~220GB - deletions were intentional, not lost work
detail: 2026-08-02 freed ~220 GB across local + T7: ~/Library/Caches/llama.cpp/ane-mtp (14 GB), /private/tmp/tessera-work-* (~1 GB), T7 dspark .bak/.prekeybak/.preswa (5.4 GB), T7 gemma-4-12B ane-prefill experiments (106 GB). All confirmed intentional by user. /Volumes/Untitled/ is the SAME physical T7 mounted via a longer mountpoint - not duplicates.

summary: test-spec-calibration.cpp model-based path aborts on main: GGML_ASSERT(has_draft || spec_mtp) at common/speculative.cpp:2344
detail: The test (tests/test-spec-calibration.cpp:185-217) sets params_dft.speculative.draft.target_model_path then calls common_speculative_init_from_params(params_dft, model_v, ctx_v). The init function asserts has_draft || spec_mtp at common/speculative.cpp:2344, but has_dft() (common/common.h:390) only checks !draft.mparams.empty(). The test only sets target_model_path, not mparams, so has_dft() returns false and the assert aborts. Same failure on main @ 7034c6ace (the has_dft() assert is in main; the test was last touched in 20f75c8cf when the spec-calib module was added). NOT introduced by the spec-consolidate agent. Suggested fix: either (a) update the test to set draft.mparams via common_base_params_to_speculative + a real drafter model load, or (b) relax has_dft() to also accept !draft.target_model.empty().

summary: Duplicate spec-calib paths: tools/imatrix/imatrix.cpp + common/speculative-calibration.cpp
detail: The spec-decoding calibration loop is implemented in two places: (1) the new common/speculative-calibration.{h,cpp} module (added in 20f75c8cf as an additive cherry-pick from tessera/spec-calib-api), and (2) the inlined version in tools/imatrix/imatrix.cpp (compute_imatrix_spec, around line 2062). The new common module is the operational path; the inlined imatrix path is dead code from the production standpoint but still compiles. The spec-consolidate agent's emission fix only touches the new module. The 20f75c8cf commit message acknowledges this duplication: 'Resolve by: either redoing the extraction in a follow-up agent that builds on current main, or leaving the new module dormant until a consumer needs it.' The duplicate is now dormant, but if either path diverges (e.g. one is updated for a new field) the other will silently emit the old shape.

summary: s2 LLAMA_KV_LAZY_CLEAR wave-3 '+0.59 GB regression' non-repro does NOT hold on current main - s2 is reproducibly a ~168 MiB WIN
detail: Re-validated commit 6f3a7495f (LLAMA_KV_LAZY_CLEAR opt-in) on current main (cherry-pick 5fa932bc0 onto df3e9c6cd). Setup: gemma-4-12B Q5_K_M, llama-bench -p 512 -n 32 -ngl 99, 5 runs per env-var setting, /usr/bin/time -l for peak RSS. n_ctx_train=262144 so the KV buffer is ~7.5 GiB; the eager clear touches it all. Results: median RSS OFF=8777826304 (8.175 GiB), median RSS ON=8601780224 (8.011 GiB), delta=-167.89 MiB (RSS drops when lazy clear enabled, opposite direction to wave-3 claim). t/s deltas: pp +2.74%, tg +3.85% (or ~0% if cold-cache runs dropped). RSS stdev was much tighter for ON (0.41 MiB) than OFF (15.08 MiB) - the lazy path is more deterministic. Wave-3 noise floor was ~50 MiB; s2's effect is 3.36x that and well outside the noise band. The wave-3 '+0.59 GB regression' was a stale-baseline artifact (different n_ctx, different system state, or different code on the OFF path) - NOT a real property of the patch. Recommendation: promote s2 to main, keep the env-var opt-in, do not flip the default yet. Lesson: 'confirmed-non-repro' entries deserve a 2nd-agent re-check on a moving baseline (3 weeks of churn since wave-3).

summary: g3 243-entry select chain produces IDENTICAL wrong Y to baseline (3.5999e+00) - 243-entry gather is NOT the bug source
detail: Replaced mb.gather(trit5_lut, selectors) with a 243-deep mb.select chain that maps each selector value 0..242 to the corresponding trit5_lut entry as I32. The MIL compiled cleanly via coremltools 9.0, the .mlmodelc loaded, and the test ran all 4 seeds with the SAME wrong values as the baseline (3.5999/3.7538/10.712/3.2781 max_abs_err). Ruled out the 243-entry const gather as the bug source. The remaining suspect constructs are: floor_div+mod4 I32 (5-way extract), tile+reshape to 5D, per-page F16 scale broadcast, outlier addback gather, or the matmul input shape. Note: 243 select ops adds MIL complexity that the ANE compiler handled fine, so 'ANE rejects complex MIL' is also not the issue.

summary: g5 2D page_scale broadcast produces IDENTICAL wrong Y to baseline (3.5999e+00) - page scale broadcast pattern is NOT the bug source
detail: Moved the per-page scale broadcast from 5D [out, pages, 1, 1, 1] over [out, pages, 32, 4, 5] to 2D [out, pages, 1] -> tile to [out, pages, 640] -> reshape to [out, in_dim_padded]. Mathematically equivalent. MIL compiled cleanly, .mlmodelc loaded, test ran all 4 seeds with the SAME wrong values as the baseline (3.5999/3.7538/10.712/3.2781). Ruled out the per-page F16 scale broadcast pattern as the bug source. Combined with g3 (243-entry gather ruled out), the remaining 3 suspect regions are: 5-way floor_div+mod on I32 axis (the mod4 chain), 4-way tile-to-5 reshape, and the I8 input shape (lane_scales).

summary: g1 pre-decomposed trits as I32 inputs produces IDENTICAL wrong Y to baseline (3.5999e+00) - 5-way floor_div+mod4 chain is NOT the bug source
detail: Pre-decomposed each u32 word into 4 selectors * 5 trits on the host (in ggml-ane.mm dispatch). The .mlmodelc input is now 4D I32 [out, pages, words, 20] (state_layout.py is 1-4 dims, so the 5D shape is flattened to 4D for the IOSurface slot and reshaped to 5D inside MIL). MIL just does sign LUT gather + scales + matmul (no 243-entry gather, no floor_div+mod4, no tile). MIL compiled cleanly, .mlmodelc loaded, test ran all 4 seeds with the SAME wrong values as the baseline (3.5999/3.7538/10.712/3.2781). Combined with g3 (243-entry gather ruled out), this rules out the floor_div+mod4 chain and the tile-to-5D reshape. Note: I8 input shape caused a bus error in the dispatch's MLFeatureValue path - confirmed via Python coremltools 9.0 predict() returning 'value type not convertible'. iOS 26 I8 multi-array is supported in the .mlmodelc but the IOSurface path doesn't handle it. The I32 fallback is over-provisioned for 0..2 trit values but functional.

summary: g1 gen2 arithmetic sign LUT produces IDENTICAL wrong Y to baseline (3.5999e+00) - 4-entry sign LUT gather is NOT the bug source
detail: Replaced the mb.gather(trit_sign_lut, trits_flat) with arithmetic: mag = cast(t!=0, fp16) - cast(t==2, fp16). For t in {0, 1, 2} this gives {0, +1, -1}, same as the sign LUT. MIL compiled cleanly, .mlmodelc loaded, test ran all 4 seeds with the SAME wrong values as the baseline. Combined with g1 gen0 (which skipped the 5-way floor_div+mod4), this rules out the 4-entry sign LUT gather. Ruled out suspects so far: 243-entry gather (g3), 5-way floor_div+mod4 + tile-to-5D (g1 gen0), 4-entry sign gather (g1 gen2), 5D page_scale broadcast (g5), 2D page_scale broadcast (g5). Remaining suspects: lane_scale cast I8->F16, F16 multiply chain, outlier addback logic, or the dequant math shape/stride. The matmul itself is correct (verified via identity test: 4x4 identity @ b = b, max diff 0.0).

summary: g1 gen3 bypasses MIL dequant via F16 W input - max_abs_err 6.58e-03 (passes 2e-2 bar) - bug ISOLATED to MIL dequant chain
detail: Replaced the MIL dequant chain entirely: the .mlmodelc input is 2D F16 w_dequant [out, in_dim_padded]. The dispatch calls dequantize_row_tessera_t640 (the C++ dequant-on-host path) to compute W in F32, casts to F16, and passes it. The MIL only does slice + outlier addback + matmul. Test ran 4 seeds: max_abs_err [6.58e-03, 8.04e-03, 1.59e-02, 6.93e-03] (all pass 2e-2 bar), max_rel_err [1.11e-01, 4.71e-02, 6.40e-02, 1.66e-01] (2/4 pass 1e-1 bar, the 2 dense cases fail by 10-66%). The F16 precision is the limit on dense cases (small reference values). Subsumed by g2 (south) which uses the same approach with a cleaner .mlmodelc structure (no extra slice/outlier addback ops in MIL) and gets bit-identical-to-dequant results on all 4 seeds. Combined with g3 and g5 evidence, the bug is in the MIL dequant chain AS A WHOLE - the exact construct within the chain that misbehaves is unknown.

summary: fused dequant+matmul on ANE: bug ISOLATED to the MIL dequant chain. Bypassing it (F16 pre-dequant on host, simple matmul on ANE) fixes parity on 256x256 (max_abs 8.6e-04 vs 3.60 baseline) and scales to 512x512 + 1024x1024.
detail: g2 (south) on integration/main @ eac8c5a13: the GGML_OP_TILE640_MATMUL_FUSED dispatch case now does the TILE640 dequant on the host (dequantize_row_tessera_t640) and passes the F16 weight + F16 B to a simple matmul bundle. 4/4 seeds pass both abs and rel bars on 256x256 dense (0xC0DE: 8.6e-04 abs / 1.89e-2 rel). Fused-vs-dequant: 0.0 (bit-identical to the dequant-on-host ANE path). g1/g3/g5 (north) collectively ruled out 7 suspect constructs (243-entry gather, 5-way floor_div+mod4, 4-way tile-to-5 reshape, 4-entry sign LUT, 5D/2D per-page F16 scale broadcast, I8 input shape, 243-deep select chain). The bug was NOT in any individual construct; it was in the MIL dequant chain AS A WHOLE. Trade-off: the FUSED op is now functionally identical to the DEQUANT op (per the architect's 'evolve, don't version' rule, the FUSED .mlmodelc replaces the FAILED fused .mlmodelc rather than coexisting). The dequant is the host prologue (same cost as the dequant-on-host path), but the bundle is simpler. 4096x4096 follow-up: g6 (south) built a per-shape test extension; the g2 path fails the rel bar on 4096x4096 (rel 0.11-0.24, bar 0.1) due to fp16 matmul precision over 4096-element dot products. The Phase 0 follow-on (ane-tile640-4096-tiling worktree) addresses this via inner-dim tiling.

summary: g6 multi-shape coverage: g2 F16 pre-dequant fix passes 512x512 (4/4) and 1024x1024 (4/4), partial on 128x4096 (3/4), fails 4096x4096 (0/4) due to fp16 matmul precision limit on 4096-elt dot product
detail: Per-shape parity test built for 4 new shapes beyond 256x256: 128x4096x1, 512x512x1, 1024x1024x1, 4096x4096x1. 4096x4096 fails rel err 0.11-0.24 vs 0.1 bar (abs err 5-13e-3 fine). Root cause: ANE fp16 matmul accumulator over 4096-elt dot product has too much rounding error vs the L0.5 fp32 reference. Same limit applies to the dequant-on-host path. The Phase 0 follow-on (ane-tile640-4096-tiling worktree) addresses this via inner-dim tiling. Test program test-ane-tile640-matmul-fused-shapes.cpp and 4 new shape fixtures are available in the g6 branch (evolve/ane-fused-dequant/g6) for future use; not merged to integration/main (non-compounding, would regress 4096x4096 ctest if added).
ref: ane-fused-dequant/best.md g6 section, integration/compound.md g6 section

summary: New run ane-tile640-precision-w1 bootstrapped - matmul precision strategies for 128x4096x1 dense rel_err 1.11e-01 to 1.66e-01 (target < 1.0e-1)
detail: Carry-forward from ane-fused-dequant: 5 individual MIL dequant constructs ruled out as the bug source; bug is in the matmul precision (fp16 dot product over 4096 inner dim), NOT in the MIL dequant chain. New gene pool: 6 matmul precision strategies - Kahan summation, smaller inner-dim tiles, rescale before fp16, int8 dot-product, two-stage matmul (split-K), fp32 accumulation throughout (compute_precision=FLOAT32). Evaluator: new harness tools/ane-mtp/eval-tile640-precision.py - 4 seeds x 1 shape (128x4096x1 dense) + control (256x256x1 dense); wall-clock ~15-20s per eval.

finding: ANE matmul precision is at the fp16 limit for the 128x4096x1 case. The current g2 (F16 pre-dequant) path achieves 7.25e-3 rel_err, well under the 1e-1 bar. The spec baseline of 1.66e-1 is from a pre-g2 state. None of the 6 candidate strategies (Kahan, smaller tiles, rescale, int8, two-stage, fp32 accumulation) improve over this baseline.
evidence: tools/ane-mtp/eval-tile640-precision.py harness on dispatch path, gene-ledger.json per-gene verdicts
applicable_to: future Tessera ANE matmul precision work

summary: v2 dynamic dispatch cost model: threshold (n_total <= 1024), not math; meta always C ref
detail: Implemented per-call cost model for the two batched v2 quant functions (decode_per_row_meta_v2, apply_outlier_addback_v2) in ggml/src/ggml-quants-v2-dispatch.h and wired it into ggml-ane.mm's GGML_OP_TILE640_MATMUL case. Cost model: (1) outlier addback: v2 iff n_total in (0, 1024]. The v2's NEON bulk fp16->fp32 path is active for n_total <= 1024 (the 4 KB stack scratch cap); above that the v2 falls back to scalar (same as C ref) and a function call is wasted. (2) meta decode: always C ref (v2 is 0.41-0.65x of C across all measured shapes on M1 Pro). The v2 dequant stays on the static rule (v2 at in_dim >= 1024, 1.30-1.63x faster than C ref). The spec's preferred approach was a math model (v2_setup_tax + v2_per_row * n_rows vs c_per_row * n_rows) but the bench data is memory-bandwidth bound at large n on M1 Pro: v2 outlier at n_rows=1024 ranges 486-6416us across runs (10x variance) and C ref ranges 483-2105us. A per-row cost model from a linear fit through (n=1, n=1024) is dominated by noise. The threshold approach pins the v2's win region to its internal NEON path boundary (n_total <= 1024), which is a hard deterministic criterion. Implementation is a hybrid path: C ref meta + v2 dequant (with pre-decoded meta) + C or v2 outlier. The C ref meta produces the pre-decoded arrays the v2 dequant needs; the C ref outlier scatters into the v2 dequant's output buffer. Tests: tests/test-ane-tile640-dispatch.cpp asserts the cost model picks at n_rows=1, 5, 6, 16, 64, 256, 1024 (plus n_total=0 no-work, n_total=1020 just-under, n_total=1024 boundary, n_total=1224 just-over) and the C ref fallbacks are self-consistent with the v2's scalar fallback. All 2 tests pass; 0 mismatches; C ref parity is bit-identical. Branch: evolve/t640-quants-v2-dynamic-dispatch off 4f2781663.

summary: HIGGS proxy L1-on-ANE wire-up landed: l1_kernel_dequant is the new default t_squared_source; legacy offline via TS_HIGGS_PROXY_LEGACY_OFFLINE=1
detail: ts_higgs_proxy_measure_l1 + ts_higgs_proxy_pack_tile640 in tools/quantize/tessera/tessera-higgs-proxy.cpp: pack each tensor to the flat TILE640 row layout with the C reference quantizer (deterministic), dequantize with the exact GGML_OP_TILE640_MATMUL dispatch semantics (v2 dequant at in_dim >= GGML_TESSERA_T640_V2_MIN_K when ggml_tessera_t640_v2_enabled(), C reference below; meta decode via ts_v2_dispatch_should_use_v2_meta, currently C ref), round-trip through ggml_fp16 (the bundle's pinned slot dtype - the F16 pre-dequant), and report t_l^2 = mean |W - W_deq| / max |W|. The estimator selects the L1 path inside ts_higgs_proxy_estimate when measurement_fn is null and the legacy env is unset; a caller-supplied measurement_fn keeps the legacy behavior bit-identical. Sidecar JSON shape is unchanged (only the t_squared_source value). Empirical L1/offline ratio ~1.41-1.55 on uniform weights (L1 captures ternary error + fp16 rounding); proxy alpha is the structural family prior, so alphas are bit-identical between sources. Test suite 180 checks (was 138): packing layout, guards, determinism, L1-vs-offline range [1.0, 2.5], v2 branch at in_dim=1024, legacy env opt-out, JSON shape, end-to-end alpha parity. v2-enabled vs v2-disabled L1 parity verified via external process runs (GGML_TESSERA_T640_V2_DISABLE=1) because ggml_tessera_t640_v2_enabled() caches the env on first read. Suite wall time 0.09s -> 3.9s (pack+dequant of every fixture tensor).
